insights.summary: Regeneron reported FY 2024 revenues of $14,033 million and net income of $2,213 million, with significant headwinds from EYLEA biosimilar competition following the May 2024 loss of U.S. regulatory exclusivity. EYLEA U.S. sales declined 17% YoY, though partially offset by EYLEA HD (20% of combined U.S. EYLEA/EYLEA HD sales). The company faces substantial regulatory, competitive, and operational challenges, including reliance on two major collaborators (Sanofi and Bayer) for 74% of net product revenue, heightened pricing pressures from government programs, and significant manufacturing capacity constraints.
keyQuotes: For the year ended December 31, 2024, EYLEA U.S. net product sales declined by 17% compared to the same period in 2023. Following the expiration of the U.S. regulatory exclusivity period for EYLEA (i.e., the period during which no biosimilar product can be approved by the FDA) in May 2024, several biosimilar versions of EYLEA have been approved by the FDA, and one such product has launched in the United States.
For the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, our product sales to two distributor customers accounted on a combined basis for 74% and 76% of our total gross product revenue, respectively.

We are substantially dependent on our share of profits from the commercialization of Dupixent under our Antibody Collaboration with Sanofi. For the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, Sanofi collaboration revenue (most of which is attributable to our share of profits from the commercialization of Dupixent) represented 32% and 29% of our total revenues, respectively.
